newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: HAVEL CONFIRMS FIRST WOMAN IN CZECH CABINET.
newsitem.headline: HAVEL CONFIRMS FIRST WOMAN IN CZECH CABINET.

text.p: President Vaclav Havel on Tuesday appointed Vlasta Parkanova as justice minister in a ceremony at Prague Castle, making her the first woman to serve in the Czech cabinet, since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993.

The ruling three-party conservative coalition led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus agreed on Monday to name Parkanova as justice minister, replacing Jan Kalvoda who resigned last month after he admitted to using an unattained "Doctor of Law" title.
Parkanova, a certified doctor of law aged 45 who was serving until now as chief of staff at the interior ministry, was nominated by the junior coalition partner, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).
Klaus has rejected any criticism of his cabinets' lack of a woman, once telling a group of foreign jouranlists that there was not a qualified woman willing to serve in the cabinet.

Kalvoda, a parliamentary deputy and a cabinet member since the coalition was formed in 1992, was the fifth member of parliament who admitted using the title of Juris Doctor without actually having qualified for it.
Out of the other four fake doctors, only one has resigned her parliamentary seat.
